articles.title: Global Market: China, Hong Kong stocks slide as oil surge fuels inflation concerns
articles.content: Asian markets saw declines in China and Hong Kong equities on Friday. Crude oil prices surged above $100 a barrel, intensifying inflation worries. Rising energy costs and liquidity pressures will influence markets near term.

articles.title: Mukesh Ambani’s long game: How Reliance could turn a 3-year spending spree into Rs 90,000 crore of free cash flow
articles.content: Reliance Industries could generate nearly Rs 90,000 crore in cumulative free cash flow over FY26-FY28 as its heavy investment cycle eases, brokerages say. articles.title: Oil shock, Treasury yield spike put Indian bonds under pressure before debt sale
articles.content: Indian government bonds experienced a decline as oil prices surpassed one hundred dollars per barrel.  The benchmark bond yield reached its highest level in five weeks during early trading.  Rising oil prices and Treasury yields pressured overnight swap rates higher.  Investors anticipate a Federal Reserve rate hike, pushing US Treasury yields upward.  New Delhi prepares to raise significant funds through a bond auction later today.

articles.title: RBI intervention blunts oil surge, shores up rupee
articles.content: The Reserve Bank of India intervened by selling dollars to prevent the rupee from reaching a record low. Surging oil prices and declining stock markets are currently pressuring the Indian currency. Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East are contributing to higher crude oil prices globally. India, heavily reliant on oil imports, faces significant economic challenges from these price increases.

articles.title: Caliber Mining and Logistics shares list at 19% premium over IPO price on BSE

articles.title: Why Swiggy shares fell over 5% today: Foreign ownership cap sparks $460 million passive outflow fears
articles.content: Swiggy shares fell after the company proposed cutting its foreign ownership limit to 49.5% from 100%, raising concerns over its eligibility for major global indices. The move could lead to Swiggy's exclusion from the MSCI Standard and FTSE indices, triggering an estimated $460 million in passive outflows, according to reports.

articles.title: HDFC Bank, 3 other bank stocks wipe out Rs 1.5 lakh crore of investors' wealth after Q1. Time to buy the dip?
articles.content: Shares of HDFC Bank, Axis Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank and Yes Bank have erased over Rs 1.5 lakh crore in market value this week following their June-quarter earnings. articles.title: Global Market: Japan's core inflation picks up in June; BOJ rate outlook keeps markets on edge
articles.content: Japan's core consumer inflation rose to 1.6% in June. This increase occurred while food prices eased and service inflation slowed. Underlying inflation, excluding food and fuel, also saw a slight decrease. Economists anticipate stronger inflationary pressures later this year due to rising energy costs. The Bank of Japan will consider these figures at its upcoming policy meeting.

Global Market: US urges BOJ to keep raising rates, flags persistent yen weakness despite narrower yield gap
articles.content: The US Treasury Department has urged the Bank of Japan to continue raising interest rates. Higher prices are impacting Japanese households' purchasing power despite wage gains. Further policy normalization by the Bank of Japan is seen as beneficial.

articles.title: Global Market: HSBC to sell Singapore insurance business to Allianz in $2.09 billion deal
articles.content: HSBC will sell its Singapore life and health insurance business to Allianz. This deal values the unit at S$2.7 billion and is expected to close in early 2027. The transaction will generate a pre-tax gain for HSBC and improve its capital ratio. Allianz gains a stronger presence in Singapore's insurance market through this acquisition. HSBC will distribute Allianz's insurance products in Singapore for fifteen years.

articles.title: South Korean shares fall over 5% on AI spending concerns and oil spike
articles.content: South Korean shares declined significantly on Friday due to AI spending concerns. Mega US tech firms' moderation in AI outlays impacted Asian chipmakers' outlook. The benchmark KOSPI index triggered a trading curb, reflecting investor caution.
